chapter: War years, Decca records and La Conga
title: Promoting Saturday dances uptown
summary: With no clubs, Machito, Mario and Federico Pagani rented ballrooms and kept bar receipts; Machito was king uptown.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: So, in other words, why ......

Before, before we were running dances because we get into La Conga, Beachcomber, and we played at the Havana Madrid, all those nightclubs that we played two-weeks, four weeks or whatever the time. We was practically-seventy-five percent of the dances that I played in New York, was promoted by myself.
Was there a reason for that, Macho?

Well, because there was no - in those days we had about maybe forty or fifty thousand Puerto Ricans and there wasn't incorporated club, there wasn't no dance every week- maybe all those like the employees of the mail, mail-people, and the whatever organization, maybe they used to run a dance, twice a year ......
I see.
..... or maybe one a year.
Uh - Huh, so it was people like you, Mario and Federico Pagani......
and Federico
....that would throw this dances every so often? Would you say it was every week?
Practically every Saturday......
Practically every Saturday, eh?
.....in different places.
Uh - Huh. What would you do, go to the owner of the place and negotiate with him?
..and rent the ballroom, sometime that we had it for free. We had the bar concession....
And he would keep the bar, the receipts from the bar?
Right, because we were so hot, we were so popular that all the ball-room owners they want me to play in the ballroom and they didn't charge me for the ballroom.
They knew you'd fill-up the place.
They even helped me to pay the publicity.
No kidding?
Yes
All right, so at that time you had bands like Montecino, Catalino and su Rumba, Madriguera......
Yeah, but Madriguera was in a different....
He was in a different bag, eh?
Different bag. He was at the La Conga or Rainbow Room or......
Not, not uptown.
Not uptown.
Uh - Huh
